user.title: General
user.description: HASIM reads the grid, solar and battery sources from the standard Home Assistant energy dashboard and compares contract types using day-ahead prices.

data_description.price_area: Nord Pool delivery area of your grid connection.
data_description.days: Number of past days to simulate (max. 365). Nord Pool provides about two months of price history without an account; HASIM caches prices daily, so the usable history grows the longer it runs.
data_description.vat: VAT percentage applied to energy prices.

fixed.title: Fixed contract
fixed.description: Prices including VAT and energy tax. Leave the import price empty to use the prices configured per grid connection in the energy dashboard.

data_description.fixed_import_price: Price per imported kWh, incl. VAT and taxes.
data_description.fixed_export_price: Compensation per exported kWh (net surplus when net metering is enabled).
data_description.fixed_net_metering: Exported kWh are subtracted from imported kWh at the import price.
data_description.fixed_standing_charge: Fixed supply costs per month, incl. VAT. Leave costs identical for both contracts at 0.
data_description.fixed_feed_in_fee: Monthly fee charged for feeding in solar power.

dynamic.title: Dynamic contract
dynamic.description: Costs on top of the day-ahead spot price. Markup and energy tax are entered excluding VAT; VAT is added automatically.

data_description.dynamic_markup_export: Subtracted from the spot price for exported kWh, excl. VAT.
data_description.dynamic_net_metering: Energy tax (and VAT on it) is only charged on net import.
data_description.dynamic_standing_charge: Fixed supply costs per month, incl. VAT.
data_description.dynamic_feed_in_fee: Monthly fee charged for feeding in solar power.

battery.title: Home battery (hypothetical)
battery.description: Simulates an additional home battery on top of your measured energy flows.

data_description.battery_investment: Purchase and installation cost, used for the payback time.
data_description.battery_grid_charging: When disabled the battery only stores solar surplus (self-consumption). When enabled it also buys cheap and sells expensive hours (arbitrage).
